facts.text: SmartGrasper subscribes to /joint_states as sensor_msgs/JointState with queue_size=1.
SmartGrasper waits for /gazebo/get_model_state and proxies it with gazebo_msgs/GetModelState.
get_object_pose returns the pose field obtained from /gazebo/get_model_state for the current model in the world frame.
SmartGrasper waits for /gazebo/reset_world and proxies it with std_srvs/Empty.
SmartGrasper waits for /gazebo/pause_physics and /gazebo/unpause_physics and proxies each with std_srvs/Empty.
SmartGrasper waits for /gazebo/set_model_configuration and proxies it with gazebo_msgs/SetModelConfiguration.

SmartGrasper.reset_world stops the hand, arm and joint_state controllers with BEST_EFFORT strictness, pauses physics, calls /gazebo/set_model_configuration, runs __start_ctrl on a zero-delay threading.Timer, sleeps 0.1 s, unpauses physics and calls /gazebo/reset_world, using none of the call results.
__start_ctrl starts hand_controller, arm_controller and joint_state_controller through /controller_manager/switch_controller.
The SmartGrasper constructor ends by calling reset_world.
open_hand and close_hand set the MoveIt named targets open and close on the hand group, plan, and execute the plan.

The reset configuration names the 15 joints shoulder_pan_joint, shoulder_lift_joint, elbow_joint, wrist_1_joint, wrist_2_joint, wrist_3_joint, H1_F1J1, H1_F1J2, H1_F1J3, H1_F2J1, H1_F2J2, H1_F2J3, H1_F3J1, H1_F3J2, H1_F3J3 and the positions 1.2, 0.3, -1.5, -0.5, -1.5, 0.0, 0.0, -0.3, 0.0, 0.0, -0.3, 0.0, 0.0, -0.3, 0.0.
The MoveIt SRDF assigns the arm group six joints (shoulder_pan_joint through wrist_3_joint) and the hand group nine joints (H1_F1J1 through H1_F3J3).
The MoveIt SRDF defines hand group state open with 0.0, -0.3, 0.0 for each finger and hand group state close with 0.0, 0.25, 0.4 for each finger.
The launch file starts Gazebo from fh_desc/launch_simulation.launch, then MoveIt move_group, gazebo2rviz and optionally RViz.
The MoveIt controller list gazebo_controllers.yaml names arm_controller and hand_controller with follow_joint_trajectory action namespaces; the arm lists six joints and the hand nine.
SmartGrasper initializes its current model name to cricket_ball.
The fh_desc launch sets the robot_description parameter and spawns the model as smart_grasping_sandbox with -param robot_description.
The Docker base image is osrf/ros:indigo-desktop-full, a ROS 1 Indigo environment.
The helper uses Python 2 print statements (print fraction) at lines 370 and 390.
The helper's header states 'Copyright (C) 2018 Shadow Robot Company Ltd - All Rights Reserved. Proprietary and Confidential.'
The repository LICENSE file is the GNU General Public License, version 3.
The smart_grasping_sandbox package.xml declares the licence GPLv3.
The six UR10 arm joints declare PositionJointInterface transmissions.
The model loads libgazebo_ros_control with gazebo_ros_control/DefaultRobotHWSim.
The hand joint H1_F1J1 declares an EffortJointInterface transmission.
hand_controller is an effort_controllers/JointTrajectoryController over the nine hand joints.
launch_simulation.launch defaults gui to true and paused to false.
launch_simulation.launch loads ur_gazebo's arm_controller_ur10.yaml, spawns arm_controller and spawns hand_controller.
The world declares ODE physics with gravity -9.81 and max_contacts 5.

determinism.notes: Event-driven recording fake with placeholder observations and no physics step, controller update or wall-clock pacing

gaps: the fake answers only the declared Gazebo services and the /joint_states observation; it runs no Gazebo, ODE, ros_control, MoveIt, TF, camera or contact simulation
the joint-state and object-pose payloads are placeholders and do not advance with the simulator; a live run must receive them from the operator's Gazebo world

arbitrary Cartesian arm motion, MoveIt planning/execution, pick/place routines, object spawn/delete and collision-matrix changes are NOT COVERED; the static rosbridge mapping cannot express the nested MoveGroup constraints or the multi-step helper routines
the fixed home and hand open/close commands use gazebo_msgs/SetModelConfiguration, which sets the named joints directly; they are not trajectory execution and do not move the arm around obstacles

unlike SmartGrasper.reset_world, these commands neither stop the controllers nor pause physics around the request, so the running arm (position) and hand (effort) JointTrajectoryControllers can drive the joints back toward their held setpoints; applied reports only Gazebo's success flag, and the helper's own open_hand/close_hand use MoveIt planning instead
/gazebo/pause_physics holds the simulation but does not cancel a pending MoveIt goal or an external ROS action client; a deployment must reconcile that native work separately
any ROS client can resume physics: the Gazebo GUI (launched by default), SmartGrasper() and its reset_world call /gazebo/unpause_physics, and the controllers then continue their goals
the controllers and joint_state_controller run inside Gazebo's update loop (gazebo_ros_control, outside the clone), so /joint_states can stop while physics is paused; the fake keeps answering
mhs.safety.reset calls /gazebo/reset_world and this package does not unpause on reset; physics resumes only through unpause_physics or another client
every binding uses the bridge's default 2 s service timeout; a Gazebo that answers later makes the call fail, and for the e-stop that means SAFE_STATE_UNREACHED with the latch held
the upstream is ROS 1 Indigo with Python 2 helpers; this package is Python 3 and speaks only the rosbridge JSON wire protocol, so live operation requires a rosbridge endpoint in that deployment

safe_state.description: Gazebo physics is paused with /gazebo/pause_physics, so the simulated UR10 and H1 hand hold still while it stays paused; the arm and hand trajectory controllers keep their goals and resume them when any client unpauses (SmartGrasper() and its reset_world do, as does the Gazebo GUI), the pause cancels no MoveIt plan or action goal, and the acknowledgement is not sensed quiescence
